purpose: Draft D8c pilot ledger (#290): raw closed-extension counting is invariant across axis-support classes and cannot support a diversity advantage. The canonical-composite variation is exploratory only; D8c is not passed.

entries.claim: For ZFA-closed base words of length 6, every base admits exactly the same eight nonempty closed extensions of length 1-2 (^v, v^, <>, ><, /\\, \\/, +-, -+), so raw continuation counts are invariant across axis-support classes. Distinct canonical composite counts vary by support (mean 3.0 / 4.895 / 6.333 / 7.0 for support 0-3), but are unmatched and quotient-dependent.
entries.formal_scope: Finite closed words of length 6 over the 8-twist alphabet; extensions of length 1-2; canonical word equivalence. The canonical-composite number is exploratory and not an independent measure of continuation opportunity. No three-axis advantage, Penrose, persistence, or physical claim.
entries.comparator: Exhaustive census in diversity_continuation.py and data/diversity_d8c_census.json.
entries.kill_condition: A closed base where the admitted extension set differs by axis support (refuting invariance), or any claim that the exploratory canonical-composite mean passes D8c without a matched measure and independent relation.
